learningObjectives.title: Popular culture and the position of women

questions.q: Which Republican president of the 1920s is associated with the phrase 'the business of America is business'?
questions.explain: Coolidge championed laissez-faire government and business-friendly policies during the mid-1920s boom.

questions.q: Which mass-produced car symbolised the growth of the American motor industry in the 1920s?
questions.explain: Henry Ford's Model T was mass-produced on the assembly line, making car ownership affordable for millions.

questions.q: Why did Henry Ford's use of the moving assembly line make cars cheaper to buy?
options: It allowed cars to be built far faster and more cheaply, lowering the price
It relied on highly paid skilled craftsmen for each car
It used expensive parts imported from Europe
It reduced the number of cars produced each year
questions.explain: Standardised, faster production cut costs per car, so Ford could sell the Model T at a low price.

questions.q: How did 'hire purchase' help to fuel the 1920s consumer boom?
options: It let people buy goods on credit and pay in instalments, boosting sales
It banned the import of all foreign consumer goods
It gave every worker free shares in their company
It fixed the prices of consumer goods by law
questions.explain: Buying 'on the never-never' meant people could purchase cars and appliances immediately, increasing demand.

questions.q: Which group largely did NOT share in the prosperity of the 1920s boom?
questions.explain: Overproduction and falling prices left many farmers in debt and poverty despite the wider boom.

questions.q: An investor borrows money to buy shares, hoping to sell them at a higher price and repay the loan. This risky practice was known as:
questions.explain: Buying on the margin meant paying only a fraction of a share's price and borrowing the rest, fuelling speculation.

questions.q: The 1922 tariff act that placed high duties on foreign imports to protect American industry was the:
questions.explain: The Fordney-McCumber Tariff raised import duties, protecting US industries from foreign competition.

questions.q: Which constitutional amendment introduced Prohibition of alcohol?
questions.explain: The 18th Amendment, in force from 1920, banned the manufacture, sale and transport of alcohol.

questions.q: Why was Prohibition so difficult to enforce?
options: There were too few agents and demand for alcohol remained very high
Alcohol was still legal to sell in licensed bars
Almost all Americans strongly supported the ban
The amendment had never actually been passed
questions.explain: A small number of Prohibition agents could not police the huge, continuing demand for illegal drink.

questions.q: Which Chicago gangster became notorious for controlling bootlegging during Prohibition?
questions.explain: Al Capone made huge profits from illegal alcohol and was linked to the 1929 St Valentine's Day Massacre.

questions.q: Why did Prohibition contribute to a rise in organised crime?
options: Banning alcohol created a huge illegal market supplied by gangsters
It made owning a gun legal for the first time
It forced all breweries to hire gangsters as guards
It gave convicted criminals the right to vote
questions.explain: The ban created enormous profits from smuggling and bootlegging, which gangs fought to control.

questions.q: A hidden, illegal bar where customers secretly bought alcohol during Prohibition was known as a:
questions.explain: Speakeasies were secret drinking clubs that flourished despite the ban on alcohol.

questions.q: The white supremacist organisation, revived in 1915, that grew rapidly in the 1920s was the:
questions.explain: The Ku Klux Klan targeted Black Americans, Catholics, Jews and immigrants, reaching millions of members.

questions.q: Why were the convictions of Sacco and Vanzetti seen as unjust by many people?
options: They appeared to be found guilty for being Italian immigrant anarchists rather than on firm evidence
They had immediately confessed to the crime
They were tried without any jury present
questions.explain: Many believed prejudice against immigrants and radicals, not the evidence, led to their execution in 1927.

questions.q: A northern European migrant finds it far easier to enter the USA than a southern European one because of a 1924 law based on nationality. This was the:
questions.explain: The 1924 Immigration Act used national-origin quotas that favoured northern and western Europeans.

questions.q: The first feature-length 'talkie' film with synchronised sound, released in 1927, was:
questions.explain: The Jazz Singer (1927) introduced synchronised speech and song, transforming the cinema industry.

questions.q: Which amendment gave American women the right to vote in 1920?
questions.explain: The 19th Amendment, ratified in 1920, granted women the vote across the United States.

questions.q: A young woman in the 1920s bobs her hair, wears short skirts, smokes in public and dances the Charleston. She would be described as a:
questions.explain: Flappers challenged traditional expectations of women through their dress, behaviour and social freedom.

questions.q: Why did cinema become hugely popular during the 1920s?
options: It offered cheap, glamorous entertainment featuring popular film stars
It was funded and strictly controlled by the government
It was the only legal place to buy alcohol
It had replaced radio, which had been banned
questions.explain: Affordable tickets and stars such as Charlie Chaplin drew tens of millions to the cinema each week.

questions.q: Why did the position of many women change during the 1920s?
options: New jobs, the vote and labour-saving devices gave them greater freedom and independence
A new law forced all women to work in factories
Women were banned from owning any property
The government paid women to remain at home
questions.explain: Wider employment, the 1920 vote and household appliances gave many women more independence and leisure.
